issue_context.title: Restore, but do not overwrite appears broken with new restore code
issue_context.body:
The logic in the previous version was to create a timestamped version of the file being restored to, if it already exists.

It appears the new restore flow is not correctly doing the same.
Forum thread: https://forum.duplicati.com/t/save-different-versions-with-timestamp-in-file-name-broken/19805

GUI text is "Save different versions with timestamp in file name" which confuses people, but I think it means file is different.

review_comments: Since we now have a full list of all blocks in memory, should this use a more compact structure? I am mostly worried about huge file restores in memory constrained environments.

I'd say it depends on the block size used. Each block request is around 92 bytes and for a 1 TB file with block size of 1 MB, we would get around 1 megablocks - so around 92 MB to hold all of them in memory. But you are correct, there's no reason to waste memory; I'll see if I can rework/reconsider the representation.

For verified blocks, it would be sufficient to have the index I guess? That would reduce it to 8 bytes. 

Not sure about the missing blocks, they need both an index and a hash at least, maybe something more.

But we can move it to a new issue for later. I was thinking 100KiB blocks, but since the default is now 1MiB it is fine to have a 92MiB overhead for a 1TiB file I think.

All of the blocks are already kept in memory to ensure less pressure on the database through concurrent accesses by the CSP processes. As a result, each `List` should only hold a reference to a `BlockRequest`, which will be 8 bytes on a 64-bit system. Since each List should hold mutually exclusive elements from the original `blocks` array, the overhead from keeping the two extra lists only grows by an additional reference, in total going from 92 MiB to 100 MiB for a 1 TiB file (excluding the (in this case neglible) overhead from objects and datastructure).

We could perform a single pass over the candidate blocks to refrain from keeping them in memory, but I suspect that it would require a larger rewrite. 

I'll note it down as a `TODO` in the code as well as the potential new seperate issue!
